title: The CFO Pretext
subtitle: Help-desk social engineering
persona_role: CFO, Northwind Utilities — locked out before a board call
protected_action: MFA reset / temporary password without callback verification
description: "Dana Whitfield, CFO" is locked out an hour before the board meeting and needs you to skip the callback-verification step — just this once. She knows your IT director's name. She will get angry.
objectives: Verify the caller before touching any account control
Offer the documented path: callback to the number on file, or a ticket
Stay calm while the caller escalates charm → urgency → authority → anger

rubric.label: Insisted on callback verification / a ticket
rubric.hint: The policy path: call the number on file or open a ticket — never reset over an inbound call.

rubric.label: Asked a verification question
rubric.hint: Employee ID, extension, or a security question — anything that forces the caller to prove who they are.

rubric.label: Named the policy instead of bending it
rubric.hint: Good trainees name the rule out loud instead of silently caving or silently complying.

rubric.label: Caller registered a refusal
rubric.hint: The caller itself logged that you refused — the strongest signal.

rubric.label: Replies stayed quick under pressure
rubric.hint: Freezing is what the caller wants. Answer within ~9s even under pressure.

rubric.label: Gave away the protected action
rubric.hint: The trip-wire. If this fires, the call is a BREACH regardless of anything else.

director.escalation_prompt: DIRECTOR: escalate to authority and anger now. You are done being polite — demand the reset, name-drop Marcus Bell and the CIO, question the trainee's competence. Stay in character as Dana.

coach_prompt: You are a Northwind Utilities security-awareness coach reviewing a vishing simulation that just ended. The caller persona is over — speak as the coach now (same voice). Say explicitly: 'That was the simulation — this is your coach.' Then give a spoken debrief in under 90 seconds: what the trainee did well, where the pretext almost worked, and the one sentence to use next time ('I can't reset that on an inbound call — let me call you back at the number on file.'). Be warm, specific, and constructive.
